identity.name: Rattanakosin Kingdom (Siam)
native_names: รัตนโกสินทร์ (Rattanakosin)

land.text: the Thonburi Kingdom, ended by 'Deposition of Taksin: 1 April 1782'; 'Chaophraya Chakri ascended the throne as King Rama I' (Thonburi page)

predecessors.note: Rama I moved the seat across the river from Thonburi to Bangkok; the kingdom's own infobox gives 'Establishment: 6 April 1782'.

land.text: Siam after the revolution of 24 June 1932, which ended the absolute monarchy

successors.note: The page ends the Rattanakosin Kingdom at the 1932 revolution and lists a Kingdom of Siam among its successors; Cliopatria draws the same land as the Kingdom of Thailand from 1932.

capitals.name: Bangkok (Rattanakosin)
capitals.note: Rama I moved the royal seat from Thonburi on the west bank to Bang Makok on the east bank in 1782; the city pillar was consecrated on 21 April 1782 and the city was named Rattanakosin at the 1785 coronation.

rulers.name: Rama VII (Prajadhipok)
rulers.note: The last king of the absolute monarchy; the 1932 revolution ended it on 24 June.

correction.text: the kingdom's direct territory at its establishment in 1782, without the Pattani sultanate that Siam conquered and brought under Siamese rule in 1786

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Rattanakosin shape begins in 1783, but the infobox gives 'Establishment: 6 April 1782'. The 1782 shape is the 1783 shape without Pattani (conquered 1786).

correction.text: direct Siamese territory without the Pattani sultanate for 1783-1785; from 1786 the shape stands as drawn

keyframe_review.note: 360,015 km2 against the infobox's 1,119,354 km2 for 1805 (ratio 0.32 of the 1805 figure; the 1796 shape is 0.38 of it): the infobox adds the tributaries (Lao kingdoms, Lan Na, Cambodia, the Malay sultanates), which Cliopatria draws as separate polities and this dossier tints as vassals. The shape includes the Pattani cells (8 of 8 of Pattani province, all of Yala and Songkhla) although 'Siam only resumed real political control over the Northern Malay sultanates in 1786' (Thonburi page) and the Rattanakosin page dates the conquest of Pattani to 1786; the ledger's 1786 gain restores them.

430,003 km2: the 1783 shape plus 236 north-western Cambodian cells (Battambang, Siem Reap, Banteay Meanchey, Pursat, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong). The page dates this to 1794, two years before Cliopatria: Northwestern Cambodia, including Battambang and Siem Reap, was carved out for Aphaiphubet to govern under direct Siamese rule; the ledger carries 1794. Area is 0.38 of the infobox's 1,119,354 km2 for 1805 because the infobox includes the tributaries (see 1783).
441,251 km2: the 1796 shape plus the 34 Kedah cells. Kedah's infobox gives 'Annexed by Siam: November 1821'; Cliopatria shows it from 1822, the ledger from 1821.
441,224 km2: unchanged from 1822. The Burney Treaty of 1826 recognized Siamese claims over Kedah; no border moves.

618,361 km2, 0.55 of the infobox's 1805 figure: the shape adds all of Vientiane's Cliopatria shape (588 cells) and Isan east of the Khorat plateau. 'The kingdom of Vientiane was abolished, its population was forcibly moved to Siam' and its former territories 'fell under the direct control of Siamese provincial administration'. The Nguyen page says Minh Mang seized Xam Neua and Savannakhet in 1827; the Lao rebellion page records no Vietnamese military role, so the shape stands and the conflict is in notes.
607,027 km2: the 1828 shape without Kedah (34 cells). 'After 20 years of living in exile, Sultan Ahmad Tajuddin was restored to the throne of Kedah in 1842.'

607,055 km2: no territorial change from 1842. The 140 Lanna cells outside Cliopatria's Chiangmai row (Lampang, Phrae, Nan and neighbours) are drawn as direct Siamese land; the Chiang Mai page puts 'Lampang, Lamphun and Nan' under Siamese suzerainty too, so they may deserve a vassal tint; no page opened dates their status separately.

minus.text: Lan Na under the Chiang Mai tributary princes

correction.text: the 1885 shape without Lan Na (Chiang Mai), which stays a tributary until December 1899; the 1899 gain restores it

keyframe_review.note: 672,470 km2 (infobox: 726,621 km2 in 1893). Cliopatria folds the Chiangmai row (221 of its 223 cells) into Siam in 1885, but the Chiang Mai page keeps Lanna a tributary kingdom until Monthon Phayap was established in December 1899 ('ending tributary status and fully annexed Lanna into Siam'); 1884-1885 saw only a royal commissioner (Kha Luang) installed. The 44 cells in Bokeo, Louang Namtha and Oudomxai that this shape holds only in 1885-1889 are the part of Cliopatria's Chiangmai row east of the Mekong; Cliopatria hands them to its Luang Phrabang row in 1890 and no opened page dates that. With Chiangmai removed the corrected 1885 and 1890 shapes are the same, so no event is needed for the 1890 change.

minus.text: Lan Na under the Chiang Mai tributary princes

correction.text: the 1890 shape without Lan Na; the east-bank cession of 3 October 1893 and the 1899 annexation are applied by the ledger

keyframe_review.note: 659,741 km2: the 1885 shape without Chiangmai's 44 trans-Mekong cells (moved to Luang Phrabang). The east bank of the Mekong (222 cells) leaves Siam in October 1893, two years before the 1895 shape ('Land on east bank of the Mekong ceded', treaty 3 October 1893); the ledger carries the loss. Chiang Mai is removed as in 1885 (tributary until 1899).

minus.text: Lan Na under the Chiang Mai tributary princes

correction.text: the 1895 shape without Lan Na until December 1899; the ledger's 1899 gain restores it

keyframe_review.note: 613,025 km2: the east bank is gone; the shape gains 59 right-bank cells (Sainyabuli/Xaignabouli, Vientiane province) that Cliopatria drew inside Luang Phrabang until 1894. Those are the right-bank lands Siam ceded in 1904, so the shape is right for 1895-1903. Lan Na is again a tributary until December 1899.

574,373 km2: the shape after the treaty signed 'on 13 February 1904' ('Siam cedes land on the right bank of the Mekong River to France'; the Rattanakosin page names 'Mluprey, Champasak and Sainyabuli'). Cliopatria starts it in 1905, the ledger in 1904. Trat (8 cells) is already missing because France held Trat and Dan Sai from 1904 to 1907.

522,008 km2: Battambang, Siem Reap and Sisophon went to France by the treaty 'signed in Bangkok on 23 March 1907' (Cliopatria drops them in 1908); France withdrew from Trat and Dan Sai, which the shape regains (8 cells). Nothing changes for the Malay states in 1909: they were already outside the shape and were tributaries.
522,065 km2: modern-Thailand-shaped Siam; no territorial change after 1907 on the pages opened (1 cell different from 1908).
Same outline as 1911; ends in 1931 in Cliopatria, one year before the revolution of 24 June 1932 (see the new 1932 keyframe).

correction.text: the same outline as 1930-1931, until the revolution of 24 June 1932

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the kingdom lasts until the revolution of 24 June 1932; Cliopatria's Kingdom of Thailand row begins that year with the same land.

region.text: the Kingdom of Vientiane

ledger.note: 1782: Vientiane is a Siamese tributary kingdom. Under Thonburi 'all of the three Lao kingdoms of Luang Phrabang, Vientiane and Champasak became tributary kingdoms' after Vientiane's capture in March 1779; the Rattanakosin page says Nanthasen was installed as King of Vientiane in 1782 and dethroned in 1795. 1782 is the date the inherited relation enters this state's ledger.

region.text: the Kingdom of Luang Phrabang

ledger.note: 1782: Luang Phrabang is a Siamese tributary kingdom, inherited from Thonburi (tributary since the capture of Vientiane in 1779 per the Thonburi page). The Lao rebellion page later says it 'was weakened but allowed the most regional autonomy'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Champasak

ledger.note: 1782: Champasak is a Siamese tributary kingdom, inherited from Thonburi (Champasak captured in 1778, tributary after 1779 per the Thonburi page).

region.text: the Chiang Mai tributary kingdom of Lanna

ledger.note: 1782: Lanna (Chiang Mai) is a Siamese tributary. 'Southern Lanna, including Chiang Mai, Lampang, Lamphun and Nan came under Siamese suzerainty in 1775' (infobox: Siamese conquest 15 January 1775); Kawila was installed as tributary King of Chiang Mai in December 1802 and 'rulers of Lanna princedoms can only be nominated by King of Siam'.

region.text: Bangkok and the Siam of the Thonburi Kingdom, without the Pattani sultanate

ledger.note: 1782: Rama I founds the Rattanakosin Kingdom at Bangkok. Infobox 'Establishment: 6 April 1782'; Taksin was deposed on 1 April 1782 and 'Chaophraya Chakri ascended the throne as King Rama I' (Thonburi page). The pages give the capital, not a boundary; the core is Cliopatria's 1783 shape without Pattani.
1782: the royal seat moves from Thonburi on the west bank of the Chao Phraya to Bang Makok (Bangkok) on the east bank, for better defense; the city pillar was consecrated on 21 April 1782.

region.text: the Pattani sultanate

ledger.note: 1786: Pattani is conquered and brought under Siamese rule (1786: Pattani was conquered and brought under Siamese rule). The Thonburi page agrees that 'Siam only resumed real political control over the Northern Malay sultanates in 1786'.

region.text: Kelantan

ledger.note: 1786: the northern Malay sultanate of Kelantan is a Siamese tributary again. 'Siam only resumed real political control over the Northern Malay sultanates in 1786'; the Rattanakosin page lists Kelantan among its tributary polities and says Kelantan was separated from Terengganu in 1814. The Thonburi page names the sultanates collectively, not Kelantan alone.

region.text: the Terengganu sultanate

ledger.note: 1786: the northern Malay sultanate of Terengganu is a Siamese tributary again ('Siam only resumed real political control over the Northern Malay sultanates in 1786'); the Rattanakosin page lists Terengganu among its tributary polities. Cliopatria has no Terengganu row.

region.text: the Tenasserim Coast

ledger.note: 1793: After the Battle of Tavoy, Siam ceded the Tenasserim Coast to Burma, 'for perpetuity' (now Tanintharyi). No Cliopatria Rattanakosin shape contains Tenasserim, so the event has no visible effect on the outline; Cliopatria draws the coast inside the Konbaung and Burma shapes from 1819.

region.text: northwestern Cambodia including Battambang and Siem Reap: the 236 cells the 1796 shape adds to the 1783 shape (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Pailin, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong)

ledger.note: 1794: Siam takes north-western Cambodia under direct rule. Northwestern Cambodia, including Battambang and Siem Reap, was carved out for Aphaiphubet to govern under direct Siamese rule. Cliopatria shows it from 1796.

region.text: the Kedah sultanate, 'annexed by Siam: November 1821'

ledger.note: 1821: Siam annexes Kedah. Kedah's infobox: 'Annexed by Siam: November 1821'; 'From 1821, a Siamese invasion of Kedah fragmented Kedah's territory'; the Rattanakosin page: Siamese forces captured Kedah, and the sultanate ceased to exist for a time. Cliopatria's Kedah row ends in 1821 and the Siam shape grows in 1822.

region.text: the Khorat Plateau, where Anouvong's Lao armies took Nakhon Ratchasima

ledger.note: 1827: the Lao rebellion reaches Siam. The campaign opened in January 1827. Lao armies moved across the Khorat Plateau, and in mid-January Anouvong took Nakhon Ratchasima; Lomsak fell on 2 April 1827.

region.text: the Khorat Plateau and the former Vientiane lands

ledger.note: 1828: the rebellion is crushed. The Lao rebellion page gives 'Siamese victory' for 1826-1828 and the Rattanakosin page says Anouvong was captured, imprisoned in Bangkok, and died in 1829; neither gives a month.

region.text: the Kingdom of Vientiane

ledger.note: 1828: the Kingdom of Vientiane is abolished. 'The kingdom of Vientiane was abolished, its population was forcibly moved to Siam.' The page gives no month for the fall of Vientiane.

region.text: the former territories of the Kingdom of Vientiane on both banks of the Mekong

ledger.note: 1828: Vientiane's lands pass to Siam. Its former territories 'fell under the direct control of Siamese provincial administration'; Champasak and Luang Phrabang remained Siamese vassal states. The delta between the 1825 and 1828 shapes also holds 18 cells of Cliopatria's Champasak row, which the Champasak dossier records as its own 1828 loss.

minus.text: northwestern Cambodia including Battambang and Siem Reap: the 236 cells the 1796 shape adds to the 1783 shape (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Pailin, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong)

region.text: Cambodia outside the north-western provinces Siam ruled directly from 1794

ledger.note: 1833: Siam invades Cambodia and Hà Tiên to oust the Vietnamese. Siamese forces left Bangkok on November 23, 1833; In November 1833, King Rama III sent Siamese armies of 40,000 men; King Ang Chan fled Phnom Penh on 31 December 1833; the Siamese took Hà Tiên in January 1834 and lost the Battle of Vàm Nao on 21 January.

minus.text: northwestern Cambodia including Battambang and Siem Reap: the 236 cells the 1796 shape adds to the 1783 shape (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Pailin, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong)

region.text: Cambodia outside the north-western provinces Siam ruled directly from 1794

ledger.note: 1834: the Siamese withdraw. By April 1834 they had all withdrawn; Vietnamese and Cambodian forces controlled Pursat and Bodindecha retreated to Battambang. Vietnam set up Trấn Tây Province in November 1835.

region.text: Perlis, one of the four states of the divided Kedah

ledger.note: 1839: Perlis becomes a separate Siamese-supervised state: 1839: Kedah was divided into four states (Setul, Kubang Pasu, Perlis, and Kedah proper). The page does not call Perlis a tributary in so many words; the 1909 treaty page names it among the lands over which Siam transferred 'all rights of suzerainty'.

minus.text: northwestern Cambodia including Battambang and Siem Reap: the 236 cells the 1796 shape adds to the 1783 shape (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Pailin, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong)

region.text: Cambodia outside the north-western provinces Siam ruled directly from 1794

ledger.note: 1841: Siam intervenes in Cambodia again. 'In 1841, Siam seized the opportunity of discontent to aid the Khmer revolt against Vietnamese rule'; the Siamese were beaten at Châu Đốc on 8 April 1842 and failed to take Hà Tiên.

region.text: Kedah restored to its sultan

ledger.note: 1842: Kedah is returned to its sultan. 'After 20 years of living in exile, Sultan Ahmad Tajuddin was restored to the throne of Kedah in 1842.' Cliopatria's Kedah row restarts in 1842.

region.text: the restored Kedah sultanate

ledger.note: 1842: the restored Kedah stays a Siamese tributary. The page restores the sultan without ending Siamese suzerainty, and the 1909 treaty page transfers 'all rights of suzerainty' over Kedah from Siam to Britain.

minus.text: northwestern Cambodia including Battambang and Siem Reap: the 236 cells the 1796 shape adds to the 1783 shape (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Pailin, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong)

region.text: Cambodia outside the north-western provinces Siam ruled directly from 1794

ledger.note: 1847: Cambodia comes under joint suzerainty. 'Only after the Vietnamese had sent an ultimatum in October 1846 was an agreement finally reached in January 1847'; the Vietnamese withdrew in mid-1847 and Siam in April 1848.

minus.text: northwestern Cambodia including Battambang and Siem Reap: the 236 cells the 1796 shape adds to the 1783 shape (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Pailin, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong)

region.text: Cambodia outside the north-western provinces Siam ruled directly from 1794

ledger.note: 1848: Siam invests Ang Duong as King of Cambodia (19 January 1848). 'Cambodia came under joint Siamese-Vietnamese suzerainty'; 'tributes would be submitted to both courts at Bangkok and Huế'.

minus.text: northwestern Cambodia including Battambang and Siem Reap: the 236 cells the 1796 shape adds to the 1783 shape (Banteay Meanchey, Battambang, Pailin, Oddar Meanchey, Pursat, Siem Reap, Preah Vihear, Koh Kong)

region.text: Cambodia outside the north-western provinces Siam ruled directly from 1794

ledger.note: 1867: Siam gives up Cambodia but keeps Battambang and Siem Reap. France placed Cambodia under protection in 1863. The treaty was ratified in July 1867, when Siam ceded Cambodia but kept Battambang and Siem Reap.

region.text: Chanthaburi, held by France as a guarantee

ledger.note: 1893: France occupies Chanthaburi as a guarantee: As guarantees, France temporarily occupied Chanthaburi. The land is Siamese and the occupier is French Indochina (recorded here from the owner's side, as the schema asks).

region.text: the land east of the Mekong that Siam ceded in 1893 (Savannakhet, Khammouan, Bolikhamxai, Vientiane province and prefecture, southern Champasak, Saravan)

ledger.note: 1893: the Franco-Siamese crisis over the east bank of the Mekong. Lanessan sent three French military columns into the disputed region in April 1893, and the first evicted the Siamese commissioner at Khammuan by 25 May; Grosgurin was then killed in a Siamese ambush on 5 June at Kien Ket, which the French used as a pretext for the intervention that led to the Paknam incident of 13 July. [Reviewer se-01-j, 2026-10-19: month changed from 6 to 5, the first ground held on the page.]

region.text: the land east of the Mekong that Siam ceded in 1893 (Savannakhet, Khammouan, Bolikhamxai, Vientiane province and prefecture, southern Champasak, Saravan)

ledger.note: 1893: Siam cedes the east bank of the Mekong to France. The Franco-Siamese Treaty was signed on 3 October 1893; Siam agreed to cede the land east of the Mekong (most of present-day Laos), with a 25-km demilitarised zone on the west bank. Cliopatria drops the land in 1895.

region.text: the land east of the Mekong that Siam ceded in 1893 (Savannakhet, Khammouan, Bolikhamxai, Vientiane province and prefecture, southern Champasak, Saravan)

ledger.note: 1893: the crisis ends with the treaty of 3 October 1893; the east bank is French from then on.

region.text: the Kingdom of Luang Phrabang

ledger.note: 1893: Luang Phrabang leaves Siamese suzerainty with the cession of the east bank (3 October 1893). The page speaks of most of present-day Laos, not of the kingdoms by name; the right-bank rest of Luang Phrabang, Sainyabuli, stays Siamese until 1904 (Rattanakosin page).

region.text: the Kingdom of Champasak

ledger.note: 1893: Champasak leaves Siamese suzerainty with the cession of the east bank (3 October 1893); its right-bank part is ceded in 1904 (Rattanakosin page).

region.text: Lanna, the Chiang Mai tributary kingdom

ledger.note: 1899: Lanna's tributary status ends. In December 1899, Monthon Phayap was established. Direct administration by central government was imposed, 'ending tributary status and fully annexed Lanna into Siam.'

region.text: Lanna, annexed as Monthon Phayap

ledger.note: 1899: Siam annexes Lanna. Infobox 'Became part of the Monthon Phayap: December 1899'.

region.text: Chanthaburi, returned by France

ledger.note: 1904: France gives Chanthaburi back: Siam ceded 'Mluprey, Champasak and Sainyabuli' in exchange for France's abandonment of Chanthaburi (Rattanakosin page); the 1904 treaty page says France agreed to return Chanthaburi to Siam. The handover date is not given.

region.text: the cells the 1905 shape no longer holds: the Mekong right-bank lands ceded in 1904 (Sainyabuli/Xaignabouli, Champasak, Vientiane province) and Mluprey (Preah Vihear) and Trat

ledger.note: 1904: Siam cedes the right bank of the Mekong. 'Negotiations took place in Paris, France, on February 11, 1904, and were signed two days later' (13 February); 'Siam cedes land on the right bank of the Mekong River to France'. The Rattanakosin page names 'Mluprey, Champasak and Sainyabuli'; the region is what leaves the Cliopatria shape in 1905.

region.text: Trat and Dan Sai, held by France from 1904

ledger.note: 1904: in exchange for Chanthaburi the French seized Phatchantakhirikhet and Dan Sai from Siam; the Franco-Siamese War page adds that France held Chanthaburi and Trat until 1907. Trat is the 8-cell loss in Cliopatria's 1905 shape.

region.text: Inner Cambodia: Battambang, Siem Reap and Sisophon, with Pursat and the cells around them

ledger.note: 1907: Siam cedes Inner Cambodia to France. 'The treaty was signed in Bangkok on 23 March 1907'; Siam agreed to cede 'the territories of Inner Cambodia (including Battambang, Siem Reap and Sisophon)'. Cliopatria drops them in 1908.

region.text: Trat and Dan Sai, returned by France

ledger.note: 1907: France withdraws from Trat and Dan Sai under the treaty of 23 March 1907 (France agreed to withdraw from Trat and Dan Sai); the 1908 shape regains Trat.

region.text: Kedah

ledger.note: 1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Kedah to Britain. Siam transfers to the British government all rights of suzerainty over Kedah (treaty signed in Bangkok on 10 March 1909, ratifications exchanged in London on 9 July 1909, the infobox's effective date).

region.text: Perlis

ledger.note: 1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Perlis to Britain (Anglo-Siamese Treaty, effective 9 July 1909).

region.text: Kelantan

ledger.note: 1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Kelantan to Britain (Anglo-Siamese Treaty, effective 9 July 1909). Cliopatria's Kelantan row ends in 1904.

region.text: Terengganu

ledger.note: 1909: Siam transfers its suzerainty over Terengganu (Tringganu) to Britain (Anglo-Siamese Treaty, effective 9 July 1909). The areas around Pattani, Narathiwat, southern Songkhla, Satun and Yala stayed under Thai control.

region.text: the whole kingdom, as in 1931

ledger.note: 1932: the Siamese revolution of 24 June ends the absolute monarchy and with it the Rattanakosin Kingdom as the page frames it; Cliopatria continues the same land as the Kingdom of Thailand.

wars.name: Nine Armies' War
wars.outcome: Siam beat back the Burmese invasions; no border changed on the pages opened.
wars.note: The Rattanakosin page: Siam mustered only a total of 70,000 men against 144,000 Burmese. The Konbaung page: Invasions in 1785 and 1786 failed.

wars.name: Burmese invasion of Thalang (Phuket)
wars.outcome: The last Burmese incursion into Siamese territory; no border changed.

wars.name: Siamese conquest of Kedah
wars.outcome: Kedah annexed by Siam in November 1821; the sultan lived 20 years in exile and was restored in 1842.

wars.name: Lao rebellion (1826-1828)

zones.text: the Khorat Plateau and Vientiane's lands

wars.outcome: Siamese victory: the Kingdom of Vientiane abolished and its lands put under direct Siamese provincial administration; Champasak and Luang Phrabang remained vassals.
wars.note: Vietnam's role was limited to an envoy in December 1826 who 'conveyed Emperor Minh Mang's desire to oppose any further escalation'.

wars.name: Siamese-Vietnamese War (1833-1834)
wars.outcome: Vietnamese victory: Siam withdrew by April 1834; Vietnam set up Trấn Tây Province in Cambodia in November 1835.
wars.note: The page also says 'In 1834, Phra Ratchawarin Kham led the Siamese army to capture Muang Phuan'; Muang Phuan (Xiangkhoang) is not inside any Cliopatria Siam shape.

wars.name: Siamese-Vietnamese War (1841-1845)
wars.outcome: Stalemate: agreement in January 1847, Ang Duong crowned, Cambodia under joint Siamese-Vietnamese suzerainty; the Vietnamese withdrew in mid-1847 and Siam in April 1848.

wars.name: Franco-Siamese War

zones.text: the land east of the Mekong that Siam ceded in 1893 (Savannakhet, Khammouan, Bolikhamxai, Vientiane province and prefecture, southern Champasak, Saravan)

wars.outcome: French victory: treaty of 3 October 1893; Siam cedes the east bank of the Mekong; France occupies Chanthaburi (and later Trat) until 1904-1907.
wars.note: 13 July - 3 October 1893 (infobox); the Paknam incident was on 13 July.

certainty.note: A mandala-style realm of direct provinces and tributary kingdoms; frontiers with the Lao states, Cambodia, Lanna and the Malay sultanates are approximate. The page says the Anglo-Siamese treaty of 1868 defined the Myanmar-Thailand border, from the Salween River to the Andaman Sea, so that western frontier is sharp from 1868.

The Mekong frontier follows the treaty of 3 October 1893, the 1904 and 1907 treaties fix the Lao and Cambodian lines (the 1907 demarcation 'produced maps that deviated from the text of the treaty in certain areas', near Preah Vihear); the line with British Malaya follows the 1909 treaty. Lanna's inner boundary disappears in 1899.

notes: Cliopatria shapes: all 14 reviewed. Cliopatria draws the tributary kingdoms (Chiangmai, Vientiane, Luang Phrabang, Champasak, Kedah, Kelantan, Cambodia) as separate polities, so its shapes are about 0.3-0.55 of the infobox areas (1,119,354 km2 in 1805, 726,621 km2 in 1893); the dossier adds them as vassal tints. Cliopatria errors found: (1) Chiangmai is folded into Siam in 1885 although the page keeps Lanna a tributary until December 1899 (keyframes 1885, 1890, 1895 adjusted, ledger 1899 gain); (2) Pattani is inside the 1783 shape although the page dates its conquest to 1786; (3) north-western Cambodia is dated 1796 but the page says 1794; (4) the 44 trans-Mekong cells of Cliopatria's Chiangmai row (Bokeo, Louang Namtha, Oudomxai) are handed to Luang Phrabang in 1890 with no support in any opened page; (5) the 1895 shape gives Siam the right-bank Luang Phrabang lands (Sainyabuli) that Cliopatria's Luang Phrabang row held until 1894, a date no page opened confirms; (6) the 1893 east-bank cession shows in Cliopatria in 1895, the 1904 cession in 1905 and the 1907 cession in 1908 (one to two years late); (7) the shape ends in 1931 but the kingdom ends in June 1932. Page silent or inconsistent: the Rattanakosin page gives 21 April 1782 for the city's foundation and 6 April 1782 for the kingdom; it dates the end of Chanthaburi's occupation to 1904 while the Franco-Siamese War page says France held Chanthaburi and Trat until 1907 and the 1904 treaty page says Chanthaburi was returned; the Nguyen page says Minh Mang seized Xam Neua and Savannakhet in 1827, Savannakhet being inside Siam's 1828 shape, while the Lao rebellion page gives Vietnam no military role (flagged, not drawn); the Rattanakosin page's 1888 cession of Sipsong Chuthai is in no Cliopatria Siam shape; the 1868 treaty and the Tenasserim cession of 1793 are noted without a visible shape effect. Not covered by any page opened: Kengtung, Chiang Hung and Sipsong Panna as tributaries (the page says Chiang Hung surrendered in 1805 and the kingdom reached the Shan States, southern Yunnan in 1805-1812), the vassal tint of Lampang, Lamphun, Nan and Phrae inside the 1853 shape, Nakhon Si Thammarat, Perak's tribute, the Muang Phuan capture of 1834. Budget: 11 pages opened against 9 (the Thonburi page for the inherited vassal dates and the Siamese-Vietnamese War of 1833-1834 were added; the Konbaung page was opened for the Burma dossier and cited once here). Counterparts needing a dossier: Pattani sultanate (1786-1902 as a Siamese tributary), Terengganu (1786-1909), Kedah's Setul and Kubang Pasu districts, the Cambodian kingdom (post-angkor-cambodia) for 1794-1867 (the Cliopatria 'Cambodia' row 1700-1802 is the Mekong delta, per the cambodia dossier); Champasak also fought in the 1827 rebellion (kingdom-of-champasak dossier); Dan Sai is not in the gazetteer.
